document.title: Afghanistan: Raising Bin Ladin With the Taliban (Islama 01750)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] Mullah Ehsanullah Ehsan, an influential member of the Taliban Inner Shura, tells embassy officials that expelling bin Laden is not a solution ('To where and how should he be expelled?'). He says the Taliban did not know where bin Laden was and would ban his activities if he were found in their areas. He argues the real problem is U.S. non-recognition of the Taliban, and claims bin Laden was invited by the Taliban's enemies and gives them no financial help.

key_claims: Ehsan said expelling bin Ladin was not the solution and appeared to bargain action on him for US recognition of the Taliban government.
Ehsan claimed bin Ladin was invited to Afghanistan by Taliban enemies before the Taliban controlled the area and that the Taliban did not know where he lived.
Stanakzai said the Taliban were working with the Saudis on a solution to the bin Ladin problem.
Stanakzai implied bin Ladin was not funding the Taliban but being fed by them.
Taliban offered US officials visits to camps in Nangarhar and Khost reportedly closed, with timing still awaited.
